SPSS-Style Typst Tables for PDF Output

spss-tables-typst.Rmd

Overview

The psych350lab package provides functions to create SPSS-style statistical tables as Typst markup. These are designed for use in Quarto documents with format: typst to produce high-quality PDF output that mimics SPSS table appearance.

Prerequisites

Quarto Setup

To use these functions, you need:

  1. Quarto installed (version 1.3+)
  2. A Quarto document with format: typst
  3. A Typst template that defines #spss_table() and #spss_table_complex() functions

Document YAML

Your Quarto document should have a YAML header like:

---
title: "My Analysis"
format:
 typst:
   template: spss-template.typ
---

Basic Usage

In Quarto chunks, use results: asis to output the raw Typst markup:


``` r
library(psych350lab)
data(superman)
typst_descriptives(superman, c("clark_height_in", "rt_critics_score"))
```

Descriptive Statistics

Basic Descriptives 

typst_descriptives(superman, c("clark_height_in", "rt_critics_score", "rt_audience_score"))

Grouped Descriptives (for ANOVA) 

typst_descriptives_by_group(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "clark_grp")

T-Tests

Group Statistics 

typst_group_stats(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "clark_grp")

Independent Samples T-Test 

typst_ttest_independent(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "clark_grp")

Paired Samples T-Test 

typst_ttest_paired(superman, var1 = "rt_critics_score", var2 = "rt_audience_score")

One-Sample T-Test 

typst_ttest_one(superman, variable = "clark_height_in", mu = 72)

ANOVA

One-Way ANOVA 

typst_anova_oneway(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "clark_grp")

Levene’s Test 

typst_levene(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "clark_grp")

Post-Hoc Comparisons

Generate Tukey HSD and/or LSD post-hoc tables:

# Both Tukey and LSD
typst_posthoc(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "type", methods = c("tukey", "lsd"))

# Tukey only
typst_posthoc(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "type", methods = "tukey")

# LSD only
typst_posthoc(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "type", methods = "lsd")

Chi-Square Analysis

Chi-Square Test 

typst_chisq(superman, var1 = "clark_grp", var2 = "tomatometer")

The output includes:

  • Pearson Chi-Square
  • Continuity Correction (for 2x2 tables)
  • N of Valid Cases
  • Footnotes about expected counts

Crosstabulation 

typst_crosstab(superman, var1 = "clark_grp", var2 = "tomatometer")

Correlation Analysis 

typst_correlations(
 superman,
 variables = c("clark_height_in", "rt_critics_score", "rt_audience_score")
)

Regression Analysis

The typst_regression() function outputs all three standard regression tables:

  1. Model Summary (R, R², Adjusted R², Std. Error)
  2. ANOVA table
  3. Coefficients table
typst_regression(superman, "rt_critics_score ~ clark_height_in + rt_audience_score")

Non-Parametric Tests

Kruskal-Wallis Test 

typst_kruskal(superman, dv = "rt_critics_score", iv = "type")

Styled Text Boxes

Use typst_box() to create styled callout boxes for writeups, tips, warnings, etc.:

# APA-style writeup box
typst_box("The results indicated a significant relationship...", "writeup")

# Tip in the margin
typst_box("Remember to check assumptions!", "tip", side = "right")

# Warning box
typst_box("Assumptions were violated.", "warning", side = "left")

Available box types:

  • "writeup" - For APA-style results paragraphs
  • "tip" - Helpful hints (margin note)
  • "warning" - Cautions and warnings (margin note)
  • "important" - Key information (margin note)
  • "note" - General notes (margin note)

Working with SPSS Data Files

When working with .sav files imported via haven::read_sav(), you can pass the original data to preserve value labels:

library(haven)

# Read SPSS file
data_raw <- read_sav("mydata.sav")
data <- zap_labels(zap_missing(data_raw))

# Tables will use value labels from original data
typst_descriptives_by_group(data, dv = "score", iv = "group", data_raw = data_raw)
typst_crosstab(data, var1 = "gender", var2 = "treatment", data_raw = data_raw)

Complete Example

Here’s a complete Quarto document example:

---
title: "Superman Analysis"
format:
 typst:
   template: spss-template.typ
---



## Descriptive Statistics


``` r
typst_descriptives(superman, c("clark_height_in", "rt_critics_score"))
```

## Group Comparison


``` r
typst_descriptives_by_group(superman, "rt_critics_score", "clark_grp")
```


``` r
typst_levene(superman, "rt_critics_score", "clark_grp")
```


``` r
typst_anova_oneway(superman, "rt_critics_score", "clark_grp")
```

## Interpretation


``` r
typst_box(
 "A one-way ANOVA revealed a significant effect of Clark height group on critics scores...",
 "writeup"
)
```

Typst Template Requirements

Your Typst template needs to define these functions:

#spss_table()

For simple tables with uniform column headers.

Parameters:

  • title: Table title
  • subtitle: Optional subtitle
  • columns: Array of column headers
  • rows: Array of row data
  • label_cols: Number of label columns (default: 1)
  • footnotes: Optional array of footnotes

#spss_table_complex()

For tables with multi-level headers.

Parameters:

  • title: Table title
  • subtitle: Optional subtitle
  • ncols: Number of columns
  • header_rows: Array of header row arrays
  • rows: Array of row data
  • label_cols: Number of label columns (default: 1)
  • footnotes: Optional array of footnotes

See the package documentation for example Typst template implementations.
